author: Reference cases for report §12.1 derived by hand where the values are exact binary fractions, plus cases computed by exact rational arithmetic in tests/reference/oracles/function-derivative.ts, which shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.
semantics: f(x) = A·x² + B·x + C with the analytical derivative f′(x) = 2A·x + B. Inputs are doubles taken at their exact values. P = (p, f(p)); Q = (p + h, f(p + h)) for the exact sum p + h. The secant slope is (f(p + h) − f(p))/h for h ≠ 0 and undefined (COINCIDENT_POINTS) for h = 0; the difference is secant slope − f′(p). slope.sign is the exact sign of f′(p); curvature is positive-curvature (A > 0), negative-curvature (A < 0), linear (A = 0, B ≠ 0) or constant (A = B = 0); vertex.x = −B/(2A), undefined (NO_VERTEX) when A = 0. Parameters are admissible when each lies in its domain interval and the double sum p + h lies in [−5, 5].
format: expected lists every quantity. A number is a valid value; a string is a category; {"undefined": code} is an undefined status with that code; {"limit": code} is a numerical-limit status; {"subnormal": value} is a valid subnormal value carrying an UNDERFLOW approximation. probe.x echoes p. Each number is the exact value rounded once to the nearest double. lines holds the drawn tangent and secant endpoints at x = −5 and x = 5 (the secant is empty when h = 0); an endpoint whose exact value is nonzero but below the double range is drawn at 0. rejected names the diagnostic the runtime reports before evaluation. An observed number o matches expected e when |o − e| <= absolute + relative·|e|; tolerance 0 is used only when every expected number and endpoint is exact. Statuses, codes, categories and rejections always match exactly. Sampled curves: x_i is the double nearest to −5 + i/40 (i = 0 … 400), and each curve value must lie within the sampling tolerance of the exact value at x_i.
